math_dag_diagnosis.mechanism: final-answer rule lets verify-corrected value override the solve answer; coder is the weakest math model and rejects nearly everything, so the DAG outcome concentrates on coder corrections -> 13-16% vs mono-large 54%. solve=medium is itself only 33% correct vs mono-large 54%: the frozen type-prior allocation (finance priors) puts the weakest model on the core reasoning node in math.
math_dag_diagnosis.dynamic_null: wrong-but-parseable answers are invisible to the deployable signals (parse/format/consistency), so dynamic has nothing to act on: +1.0pp CI[+0.0,+0.03] Help1/Harm0

RQ1_stage_complementarity.mbpp: node oracle evidence pending per-node table; type-prior beats always-medium
RQ1_stage_complementarity.math500: type-prior allocation fails: node router 13% vs mono 54%

RQ2_node_vs_query.math500: -37.0pp CI[-48.0,-26.0] (frozen priors do not transfer across domains)

RQ3_feedback_dynamic.math500: +1.0pp CI[+0.0,+3.0] Help1/Harm0 (parse/consistency signals cannot see value errors)

cross_domain_rq.generalization_verdict: dynamic-adaptation value is signal-dependent, not domain-universal: it replicates decisively where the deployable failure signal is deterministic (code), and vanishes where the signal is only validity/consistency (math). Allocation priors are domain-specific: finance type priors fail on math.

protocol_boundaries.math_dag: analyze(large)->solve(medium)->verify(coder), final = verify-corrected value when verdict=no (frozen rule); one-shot, no post-hoc re-tuning
protocol_boundaries.no_gold_runtime: both domains; mbpp release has no reference solutions at all
